# Game model (ARC-AGI-3 style, 8 levels)

## Board
- 512x512, cell size = 8px. Bottom strip = UI/progress bar area.
- Only ACTION6 (click) is available.

## Objects
- **Snakes/bars**: 3-cell-wide colored bars. One end has a GRAY cap (= tail/anchor, fixed).
  The other end is the head. A dark-red cell sits in the middle line, **second cell from the head**.
- **Target**: hollow dark-red diamond outline (4 cells around an empty center cell).
- **Control boxes**: gray-bordered panels holding 2 icon buttons of a snake's color.
  Icons "C" / "Ɔ" = grow LEFT / grow RIGHT. Icons "∩" / "∪" = grow UP / grow DOWN.
  Panel color identifies which snake it drives.

## Rules learned
- One click on a direction button grows that snake **3 cells** in that direction
  (head advances 3; red marker stays 2nd from head).
- Level is solved when a snake's red marker lands exactly on the diamond's empty center cell.
  (Level 1 needed BOTH snakes on their own diamonds; completion fired on the last one.)
- Distance to travel = (diamond center coord - red marker coord)/8 cells, must be a multiple of 3.

## Level 1 solution (13 clicks)
Green bar grew right 7x, yellow bar grew down 6x.

## Level 2 (in progress)
Purple walls appear (obstacles). 4 snakes (orange, cyan, yellow, green) in one cluster,
4 control panels at bottom, one diamond target.

# ARC-AGI-3 puzzle: telescoping-arm / "reach the diamond" (8 levels)

## Interface
- Only ACTION6 (click) is ever available. No RESET needed.
- Board is 64x64 cells of 8x8 px. col = x/8, row = y/8. Click target = col*8+4.
- Control panels sit in the lower part of the screen. Each panel is colored like an arm and
  holds TWO icon buttons: **first/left(or top) icon = RETRACT (-3), second/right(or bottom) = EXTEND (+3)**.
  Icons "C"/"Ɔ" (horizontal pair) or "∩"/"∪" (vertical pair) — orientation is cosmetic.

## Objects
- **Arm segment**: bar 3 cells wide, with a 3-cell GRAY cap at its fixed (base) end.
  Body grows away from the cap, 3 cells per click. Body length L changes by ±3; minimum seen = 2.
- **MARKER**: single dark-red cell in the middle line of a segment, ALWAYS the 2nd cell from the head.
- **TARGET**: dark-red diamond outline (4 cells) with a hollow center cell.
  Level advances when every marker sits exactly on a diamond center.
- **Chains**: a segment's cap may be mounted on the head of another segment (perpendicular).
  Moving a parent moves all descendants rigidly. Base = segment whose cap touches nothing.
  Some chain links are colorless (#CCCCCC white) with NO panel: fixed length, act as movable walls.
- **Walls**: purple (#A356D6) and the white links. COLLISIONS ARE ENFORCED: a click that would
  make any piece overlap a wall/other piece is rejected (no state change, wasted action).
  Overlapping a diamond's outline cells is allowed (diamonds are drawn on top).

## Method that works
1. Read the board as a 64x64 cell map (read_pixels, region 0,0,512,512, 64x64) and parse carefully.
   (Beware miscounting long run-length strings — verify suspicious areas with small targeted reads.)
2. Identify each arm: cap position/orientation, body length L, and parent (cap adjacent to a head).
3. Write parametric formulas for every piece's occupied cells in terms of all L's.
4. Marker coordinate must equal diamond center; each arm's reachable coords are ≡ start (mod 3).
   Solve for required L's, then order the moves so no intermediate state collides.

[After action · write GUIDE.md]
# ARC-AGI-3 "telescoping arm" game — SOLVED (8/8)

## Interface
- Only ACTION6 (click) is ever available; no RESET needed. Board = 64x64 cells of 8px (col=x/8, row=y/8; click at col*8+4).
- Panels at the bottom/edges. A "C/Ɔ" pair = RETRACT (first icon) / EXTEND (second icon), ±3 cells per click.
  A "+" icon panel = ROTATE that segment 90° CCW (RIGHT→UP→LEFT→DOWN→RIGHT); descendants rotate with it.
- A panel drives EVERY arm of that colour simultaneously.
- Blocked clicks are rejected (state unchanged, often frame_count=2) — they still cost a turn.

## Objects
- **Segment**: 3-cell-wide bar with a 3-cell GRAY cap at its fixed end; body grows away from the cap.
- **MARKER**: dark-red cell in the middle line, always the 2nd cell from the head.
- **TARGET**: dark-red diamond outline with hollow centre. Level completes when every diamond centre holds a marker.
- **Chain**: a child's bar occupies the 3 rows/cols just beyond the parent's HEAD, rotated 90°;
  its cap sits at the end aligned with the parent's near side. Base = segment whose cap touches nothing.
  Colourless (#CCCCCC) links have no panel: fixed length, act as movable walls.
- **Walls**: purple (#A356D6) and white links. Collisions are enforced against walls and other pieces,
  including same-colour arms. Diamonds are NOT obstacles. UI panels are NOT obstacles.
- Rotations/extensions may be CLIPPED at the board edge (allowed, not blocked).
- Rotation to a 180° (fold-back) relative angle is usually self-overlapping → the game SKIPS it to the next valid orientation.

## Method
1. Read the board as a 64x64 cell map; verify suspicious runs with narrow 1-row/1-col reads (long strings are easy to miscount).
2. Identify each arm: cap cell block, direction, length, parent.
3. Write parametric formulas for every piece in terms of all lengths; marker coordinate must equal a diamond centre.
   Reachable coordinates are ≡ start (mod 3).
4. Solve for the required lengths, then ORDER the moves so no intermediate state collides
   (park blockers in gaps; move a long arm only along a corridor that fits its whole sub-tree).

[After action · message]
Game complete — **8/8 levels solved, terminal state WIN**.

Key model that carried through all levels (now saved in GUIDE.md):
- Arms are 3-wide bars with a fixed gray cap; each click extends/retracts by 3, and the dark-red marker always sits 2nd from the head.
- Arms form kinematic chains (child mounted perpendicular on parent's head), so parents move whole sub-trees rigidly.
- A colored panel drives *every* arm of that color; "+" panels rotate a segment (and its descendants) 90° CCW.
- Collisions with walls and other arms are strictly enforced, so the hard part is ordering moves — parking blockers in wall gaps and only sweeping long assemblies through corridors tall/wide enough for the entire sub-tree.
